sections.overview: Riftia pachyptila is a large deep-sea annelid living around hydrothermal vents in the eastern Pacific.
sections.identification: It lives inside a pale tube and displays a bright red plume; adults can reach about two metres.
sections.habitat: It forms dense clusters beside vent openings on the Galápagos Rift and East Pacific Rise.
sections.diet: Adults lack a digestive tract and receive nutrition from sulfur-oxidizing bacteria housed in a trophosome.
sections.behavior: Vent colonies can die when fluid flow stops, while larvae may colonize newly active vents.
sections.reproduction: Larvae hatch without symbiotic bacteria and acquire them from the surrounding water after settlement.
sections.ecology: Its bacterial partners use chemical energy rather than sunlight, supporting life in vent ecosystems.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted describe its ecology but do not provide a conservation assessment for this species.
